newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds flat ahead of bond, Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds flat ahead of bond, Greenspan.

text.p: Argentine bonds opened flat Tuesday with investors marking time ahead of the pricing of a $2.0 billion global bond and comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"It will be a news-filled day -- the market is waiting for the bond and for Greenspan," said a dealer at a large local bank. "Otherwise the underlying trend remains firm."
Argentina's 20-year global bond was expected to fetch interest slightly above 11 percent and be priced at around 475 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
In Washington, Greenspan was due to brief the Senate at 1000 EDT (1500 GMT) on the state of the U.S. economy.
"We don't expect any major surprises but the U.S. markets are going to dissect every phrase of his speech, so we could see some choppy trading," another dealer said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was unchanged from Friday at 125.20 while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 which is traded abroad inched up 1/8 to 89.40.
Local bonds went untraded Monday due to the closure of the U.S. Treasuries market on Martin Luther King Day.
